title: Large Files, Object Storage & CDNs
summary: Keep multi-gigabyte uploads and global media egress off your stateless API servers.
body:
Never stream large binary payloads through application servers or store blobs inside relational tables. Split control-plane metadata from data-plane byte transfers.

## Control plane vs data plane
- Client calls your API with file metadata (`name`, `size`, `sha256`, `content_type`).
- API authenticates, records a `PENDING` metadata row, and returns short-lived pre-signed object storage URLs.
- Client uploads or downloads bytes directly against object storage or a CDN, while object-store event notifications mark the upload `READY`.

## Chunking, resumability, and deduplication
- Split large files (`100 MB` to `50 GB`) into fixed or content-defined chunks (`4-8 MB`).
- Track each chunk's `sha256` and upload state so dropped mobile connections resume only unfinished chunks and small file edits upload only changed blocks.

## Global delivery and video pipelines
- Transcoding DAG: split uploaded video into short segments encoded in parallel across multiple resolutions and bitrates.
- Adaptive bitrate (`HLS` / `DASH`): serve a manifest plus immutable `2-6s` media segments so players switch quality smoothly as bandwidth fluctuates.
- Edge caching and origin shielding: cache popular immutable segments and daily snapshots at CDN POPs with an origin shield tier so cache misses coalesce before hitting object storage.
